plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: Cascading chains of fragrant, pea-like flowers drape pergolas, walls and old trees in a lilac-violet curtain. The blooms open before or just as the new leaves unfurl, and bees crowd around them.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-spring, typically April to May in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens
plants.location: Native to China; widely grown in gardens across Europe and the eastern United States
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines can live for well over a century. Their twining stems tighten with age and can crush the supports they climb.

plants.name: Syringa vulgaris
plants.description: Dense, cone-shaped clusters of tiny four-petaled flowers release one of spring's best-loved perfumes. The shrubs reach full bloom as the weather warms, and they often announce the end of the cold season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to late May in cool temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Gardens across the northeastern United States, Canada and northern Europe
plants.funFact: Lilac belongs to the olive family. Its flowers are edible and have a floral, slightly citrusy taste.

plants.name: Chrysanthemum morifolium
plants.description: In the Southern Hemisphere's autumn, garden chrysanthemums put on a rich display of full, layered blooms. Their warm tones suit the cooling days.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn in the Southern Hemisphere, roughly March to June
plants.location: Gardens in southeastern Australia, New Zealand and temperate South Africa
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums have been cultivated in China for more than 2,000 years. They are among the flowers honored in Japan's Imperial seal.
